title: Yves Missi Destroys Jaren Jackson Jr. So Hard The Cameraman Forgot The Game Was Still Going [VIDEO] - NewsBreak
text:
By Shabiha Akter ,
51 minutes ago
Yves Missi and Jaren Jackson Jr (Photo By X/@PelicansNBA) The New Orleans Pelicans’ struggles continued even after the dismissal of head coach Willie Green, who was let go following the team’s rough 2-10 start . On Wednesday night, the Pelicans fell 133-128 to the Memphis Grizzlies at Smoothie King Center. This loss dropped them to 3-16 on the season, with nine losses in their last ten games.
Despite the defeat, one moment involving young center Yves Missi caught widespread attention. Even the Pelicans’ social media team couldn’t resist highlighting it.
In the second quarter, Missi matched up against Jaren Jackson Jr. on a drive to the basket. His defense forced Jackson into a missed layup and sent the Grizzlies star crashing to the floor. The sequence was so eye-catching that the broadcast camera lingered on both players instead of following the next play in transition.
Missi, who saw an ejection from their game against the Portland Trail Blazers , wrapped up the night with six points, six rebounds, and six assists. All five Pelicans starters reached double figures, yet the effort still fell short of producing a much-needed victory. Zion Williamson contributed 17 points, Jose Alvarado led the team with 24, and Saddiq Bey added 18 in the loss.
Trey Murphy Praises Yves Missi’s Progress Yves Missi (Image Credits: Imagn) Recently, teammate Trey Murphy spoke extensively about Missi’s development and competitive spirit.
“I think he is figuring it out. This is year 6 of him playing basketball total… He is in NBA games contributing playing major minutes. There are people playing since they were 3 years old that still dont play with that amount of fight and effort ,” Murphy said.
Missi is in his second season with New Orleans after being selected 21st overall in the first round of the 2024 NBA Draft. During his rookie campaign, he averaged 9.1 points, 8.2 rebounds, and 1.4 assists across 73 games. So far this year, he is posting 6.1 points, 5.4 rebounds, and 1.4 assists through 14 games.
